title: People Are Selling One Prompt Websites for $1K+ (Full Tutorial)
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The speaker repeatedly endorses Ouijic, mentions its 2.0 release, and directs viewers to try it; sponsorship is not stated.

stated_problem.quote: But before I open, I need a good-looking website, and I don't have one yet.
stated_problem.speaker: Unidentified guest

idea.name: Secret Pickleball Club
idea.one_liner: A pickleball club offering court bookings, player competition and merchandise to members, with revenue from bookings and merch.
idea.customer: Pickleball beginners, competitive players and casual players.
idea.offer: Club activities, court booking, a leaderboard and member merchandise.
idea.revenue_model: Paid court bookings and merchandise upsells; specific fees are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: All right, I am starting a business called Secret Pickle Ball.
I need a court booking system, a leaderboard so people can compete with their scores, and a merch section so I can upsell.

claims.claim: The speaker hopes the AI-built site will save $3 to $5,000 in website designer costs for this business.
claims.quote: Because the hope is I can save $3 to $5,000 by not having to pay a fancy website designer, and I can have AI do it all for me.

claims.claim: The speaker says the site would save five grand if it works.
claims.quote: If this works, I save five grand.

claims.claim: The speaker says about two-thirds of site visitors use mobile devices.
claims.quote: I know that about twothirds of website visitors are looking at that website on a mobile device.

acquisition_channels.details: A public-facing club website with join and booking functions; no other acquisition channel is stated.

ideas.delivery: The club runs pickleball activities and court bookings, maintains a leaderboard and sells merchandise; the website is built with an AI website builder. Venue operations and merchandise fulfillment require physical work.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to member and booking data; PECR applies to electronic marketing. The DMCC Act may apply if memberships are sold as recurring subscriptions.

stated_problem.quote: Maybe it's a pizza restaurant where they can't know through their current system if their customers want pickup or delivery and it's a manual process and they have to call.
stated_problem.speaker: Unidentified guest

idea.name: AI-assisted web design agency
idea.one_liner: Build and sell custom websites to businesses, using an AI website builder to deliver quickly and charge per client.
idea.customer: Small businesses, including restaurants in an industry the agency understands.
idea.offer: Custom websites with features such as online ordering, booking, payments and lead handling.
idea.revenue_model: Per-client website fees; the speaker suggests charging thousands of dollars, with no verified sales shown.

key_quotes.quote: You would like to make and sell websites to other businesses.
Remember, we're charging for the value that we create, not for the amount of time that we spend.
You can still charge thousands of dollars per client.

claims.claim: The speaker says there are 76,000 pizza shops in the United States as a potential industry market.
claims.quote: I used to work for a pizza business and there are 76,000 pizza shops in the great United States of America.

claims.claim: If a client dislikes a first website, the speaker says four more prompts can generate four new websites.
claims.quote: If they don't like the first website you build, four more prompts gets you four new websites.

claims.claim: The speaker contrasts that with four hours of manual work for one to two more websites.
claims.quote: Whereas before you had to spend four more hours building one to two more websites.

claims.claim: The speaker uses $3,000 as an example of a competing agency's website price.
claims.quote: If another website design agency is charging $3,000 and they're doing it inefficiently by hand, just because you're doing it more efficiently doesn't mean you should charge less.

claims.claim: The speaker says the builder can make websites in minutes rather than months.
claims.quote: With tools like Weedic, you can build in minutes, not months.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests charging thousands of dollars per client.
claims.quote: You can still charge thousands of dollars per client.

claims.claim: The speaker says regenerating a section uses five credits.
claims.quote: With this button here, I can use five credits to regenerate this whole section.

claims.claim: The speaker says websites can be built in minutes, or in one minute in the demonstrated case.
claims.quote: You can build websites in minutes or in minute in this case.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests charging thousands of dollars per client.
claims.quote: You can charge thousands of dollars per client.

claims.claim: The speaker says the builder's first website is free.
claims.quote: So, go ahead and start with that and know that your first website is free.

acquisition_channels.details: The speaker recommends asking business owners generalized questions to uncover problems; no specific channel for finding or winning clients is stated.

ideas.delivery: The solo agency owner discovers business problems, generates and revises websites with an AI builder, then works with clients on changes and publishing. Ongoing hosting and support arrangements are not stated.

prices: five credits to regenerate a section

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to prospect and client personal data. If using electronic marketing, PECR rules apply; cold email is allowed only to limited companies with an opt-out, and cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS. Recurring website subscription billing may engage the DMCC Act.

stated_problem.quote: So, I want to make a pizza website and I want it to have payments enabled so that they don't have to go through Door Dash.
stated_problem.speaker: Unidentified guest

idea.name: Secret Pizza
idea.one_liner: A Dallas pizza restaurant selling pizza through direct online ordering for pickup or delivery, keeping orders off DoorDash.
idea.customer: Local pizza buyers, with the demo targeting parents aged 25 to 55.
idea.offer: Pizza ordered and paid for through the restaurant's own website.
idea.revenue_model: Direct pizza sales; menu prices are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: It needs to have payments integrated so people can pay for and order food.
Also highlight some fake fivestar reviews that I can swap with real ones.

So, yes, we want people to be able to order, but really we just want potential customers to see the founders to see that they're local to Dallas, to see that they're loved by others with their fivestar reviews.

claims.claim: The demo site was asked to show fake five-star reviews until real reviews could replace them.
claims.quote: Also highlight some fake fivestar reviews that I can swap with real ones.

claims.claim: The demo targets parents aged 25 to 55; the transcript repeats and joins the age range as transcribed.
The speaker says the demo website took one minute to create.
claims.quote: It took 1 minute to create this website.

acquisition_channels.details: The demo website uses local-founder credibility and reviews to persuade visitors to order directly; no source of site traffic is stated.

ideas.delivery: The restaurant prepares pizzas and fulfills orders by pickup or delivery; its website takes online orders and payments. The founders are shown on the homepage as a local credibility signal.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If adapted to the UK, UK GDPR applies to order and contact data; food safety, business registration and allergen information rules apply to prepared food sales.
